actions: Built a reproducible decision-statistic mismatch microbenchmark with deterministic paired binary scoring and runtime fingerprint capture.
Derived a machine-checkable public fixture from vLLM issue #51187 showing response/logprob-object mismatch with no emitted-token divergence in two scoped workloads.
Read primary/current vLLM reproducibility evidence including merged PR #51292 and official batch-invariance material.
Analyzed the NeurIPS 2025 numerical nondeterminism paper using its PDF and screenshots; connected runtime-induced output divergence to changed final answers and benchmark accuracy.
Added an analyzer that locates first token divergence relative to the exact canonical score-certificate boundary and separately measures score-pair and oriented-sign changes.
Checkpointed all claims with exact scope and advanced the role-local LATEST pointer.
main_observation: Reproducibility mismatch must be measured as a hierarchy rather than one raw-output bit. A public vLLM trace has 28.44%-42.73% response/logprob mismatch with zero token divergence, while separate primary evidence shows runtime-induced numerical/token divergence can change final answers and aggregate accuracy. The protected exact contract for the current paired evaluation remains the deterministic oriented sign (plus any downstream state transition), and the new tooling measures where divergence crosses into that decision boundary.
blockers: No compatible GPU/vLLM runtime is available inside this automation environment, so the new microbenchmark could not yet generate an independent live repeated-inference dataset.
termination_cause: current invocation checkpointed after substantive public-source research and role-local artifact construction; frontier remains nonempty
exact_next_action: Obtain a public raw repeated-inference artifact with actual token divergence or execute the benchmark on a compatible GPU/vLLM runtime, then use the divergence analyzer to measure first-token divergence versus certificate, direct deterministic score mismatch and paired oriented-sign mismatch under the same fingerprint.
